title: Lecture day, serve reps, and club meeting
text:
I started with an 8:30 a.m. chemistry lecture and felt half-awake until the professor got into reaction mechanisms that finally clicked for me. After class I stayed in the library for two hours to rewrite my notes and build a study guide for Friday's quiz, then grabbed lunch with my roommate and talked about our summer internship worries.

In the afternoon I got an hour on court and focused on first-serve location plus two-ball patterns after the serve. My timing was shaky at first because my legs felt heavy from yesterday, but it improved once I stopped trying to hit too hard and just committed to margin. I also played a short practice set and lost it mostly on rushed forehands.

Tonight was our campus film club meeting, so I skipped doom-scrolling and went. We debated a documentary for almost an hour, then I came back to the dorm, stretched, and made a quick yogurt-fruit snack before planning tomorrow.

title: Rainy day treadmill and coding lab
text:
Rain canceled outdoor practice, so I moved training indoors with treadmill intervals and a mobility circuit in the rec center. It wasn't exciting, but I got a solid sweat and my hips felt better by the end.

Most of the day was academic mode: coding lab, office hours, and then finishing a problem set with two classmates in the engineering building. We got stuck on one bug for almost forty minutes before realizing we had mismatched variable names, which was painful but kind of funny after the fact.

I ended the night playing guitar in the common room for a little while and then meal-prepped pasta, roasted vegetables, and chicken so I don't rely on vending machine snacks this week.

title: Doubles practice and campus event
text:
I had team doubles drills today and worked on return positioning and poach timing. Coach kept reminding me to trust my first move and stop hesitating in the middle, which helped once I committed. We played points with sudden-death deuce and I won more net exchanges than usual.

After practice I had a statistics discussion section and then spent an hour at the student center printing a poster for our intro psychology project. The printer jammed twice, but we eventually got it done.

At night I met friends at a campus culture festival, tried way too much food, and stayed longer than planned because there was live music. I got back late, drank water, and wrote down three tennis notes before sleeping.

title: Match nerves and study marathon
text:
Played a match this afternoon and lost in three sets after being up a break in the third. I served well early, then got passive and started rallying without purpose when things got tight. The best part was that I kept competing instead of mentally checking out, even when momentum flipped.

I basically lived in the library afterward for a long study block with noise-canceling headphones. I reviewed bio flashcards, edited a history paper draft, and submitted a discussion post ten minutes before the deadline.

No real cooking energy left, so I did a simple dinner and tea, then watched one episode of a comedy show with my floor before bed.

title: Recovery focus and pottery class
text:
I took a lighter tennis day with basket serves and rhythm rallies just to keep feel without overloading. Main cue was keeping my non-dominant hand active longer on takeback and finishing higher on the backhand.

The bigger priority was recovery: easy bike, foam rolling, and extra hydration because my shoulders were tight. I also actually ate breakfast before class for once, which made my afternoon energy way steadier.

In the evening I went to beginner pottery as a break from school stress. My bowl came out crooked, but it was fun to do something with my hands that wasn't typing or holding a racquet.

title: Group project chaos and late practice
text:
My morning got consumed by group project planning because one teammate changed our presentation outline at the last minute. We had to rebalance slides and rehearse transitions between classes, so lunch became a granola bar and coffee situation.

I finally got on court in the evening and did a compact session: serves, return reps, and a short points game. Even though I was tired, I competed better than expected and stayed disciplined with crosscourt patterns before changing direction.

After practice I called my parents, folded laundry, and listened to a podcast while organizing my week. Nothing glamorous, but it felt like a real college life maintenance day.

title: Weekend tournament and friend birthday
text:
Tournament day. I won my first match in straight sets by serving to bigger targets and taking fewer low-percentage forehands. Second match was a grind and I lost in a third-set tiebreak, mostly because my first-serve percentage dropped late and I rushed second-ball decisions.

I refueled with a rice bowl and fruit, then took a long walk back to campus to clear my head instead of replaying every missed shot.

At night I still went to my friend's birthday dinner and tried to be present instead of stuck in match mode. We ended up playing board games in the dorm lounge, and I laughed more than I expected after a frustrating loss.

title: No tennis Sunday with academics
text:
No court today. I needed a reset, so I slept in, cleaned my room, and did a full calendar check for midterms, assignments, and practice blocks.

Most of the afternoon was reading for literature class plus outlining an essay thesis. I also had a quick Zoom study session with my cousin, who helped me tighten my argument structure.

For movement I did a short yoga flow and a walk around campus while listening to an indie playlist. Dinner was simple stir-fry and leftovers packed for tomorrow.

title: Coach lesson and creative break
text:
Had a one-on-one lesson with coach and we focused on transition balls and first volley control. We repeated approach patterns until my spacing improved, then played point-start scenarios from neutral balls. I left with clear homework: recover faster after wide forehands and commit to the first volley target.

Between classes I finished calculus homework and met with my advisor about balancing my course load next semester with travel weekends for tennis. That conversation helped because I was feeling behind on everything.

Later I spent an hour editing photos from a campus walk for fun, which was surprisingly relaxing. I ended the day with protein, vegetables, and a lot of water.

title: Exam prep, cafeteria choices, and short hit
text:
Big exam week energy. I did a focused morning study sprint with practice questions, then went to class and realized I actually understood more than I thought.

I squeezed in a short evening hit, mostly return timing and serve rhythm, and kept intensity moderate so I wouldn't fry my brain before tomorrow. The session was brief but useful for confidence.

Cafeteria dinner could have gone off the rails, but I picked grilled protein, rice, and salad, then grabbed a cookie anyway because balance. After that I reviewed flashcards with friends and we did a quick walk break before heading back to the dorm.
